title: FQHC Interpretation Billing: PPS, T1013, and AI Use
summary: Review FQHC interpretation billing under Medicare PPS, Medicaid variation, T1013, documentation, telehealth, and AI reimbursement checks.
body_markdown:
###


Medicare FQHC PPS pays for qualifying encounters under current CMS rules, and interpretation does not by itself create a separate qualifying encounter. FQHC finance teams should verify the underlying service and current CMS billing instructions before forecasting payment.


###


Do not assume T1013 covers AI interpretation because the code describes sign-language or oral interpretation in 15-minute units. An FQHC should obtain current written guidance from each Medicaid agency or managed care payer on eligible methods, qualifications, units, modifiers, and billing entities before submitting an AI-related charge.


###


Use committed operating funds, grants, and verified contract payments as the base budget when interpretation coverage is uncertain. Keep Medicare cost reporting, Medicaid rate-setting, grant accounting, and potential claims on separate lines, and treat unconfirmed interpretation reimbursement as zero in the base forecast.


###


Link the interpretation record to the qualifying encounter and retain the service date, delivery method, vendor or interpreter identifier, duration or units when required, authorization, and relevant payer fields. In a United States FQHC workflow, billing staff should compare the record with the current payer policy before submission.


###


No, Opalite’s pricing and workflow capabilities do not prove that a payer will reimburse AI interpretation. Opalite supports 150+ languages and dialects and does not charge for hold or silent time, but each FQHC still needs written payer guidance before counting reimbursement.
